question: of the pairs that become identical only once accents are stripped, which are genuine accent variants and which are an artefact of two notations?
why_it_matters: typing all of them as accent variants would invent 150 textual variants that are notation artefacts; typing none of them would erase 23 real ones. The discriminator is the measured notation class, not a guess.

verdict.INCOMPATIBLE_NOTATION_CLASSES: 150 pairs -- 81 AV-RV and 69 SV-YV. GRETIL's Atharvaveda marks tone with acute and grave; GRETIL's Rigveda marks it with macron-below and vertical-line-above; the Samavedic source marks none at all. Two texts in different notations CANNOT agree above ACCENT_INSENSITIVE, so for these pairs that level is the comparison ceiling and the right claim is EXACT_PARALLEL_OF with no accent assertion. The live graph already types all 150 that way and is correct.
verdict.SAME_NOTATION_DIFFERENT_ACCENTUATION: 21 pairs -- 15 AV-AV and 6 YV-YV. One edition, one notation, different marks placed. These are real accent variants and are typed VARIANT_OF / ACCENT_PLACEMENT.
verdict.SAME_NOTATION_SAME_MARK_COUNTS: 2 pairs. Same mark inventory and same per-mark totals, so the difference is in mark POSITION rather than count. Still a real accent variant; the per-mark counter simply cannot name it, and that limit is stated rather than rounded away.
